facts.text: The spawn_diffboat launch defaults the model namespace to diffboat and runs diff_control_heading.py inside that namespace.
diff_control_heading.py publishes thruster_command (sensor_msgs/JointState) and move_usv/result (std_msgs/Float64), and subscribes to state and move_usv/goal as nav_msgs/Odometry.
thruster_ctrl_msg names the two thruster entries fwd_left and fwd_right and sets their JointState positions to rudder_ctrl() + 100 and -rudder_ctrl() + 100, clamping only values below zero.
verify_result updates only result.data from the target_distance and desired_distance comparison; the thruster message is built separately in thruster_ctrl_msg.
The heading controller loop runs at rate_value 10 Hz and publishes both topics every iteration until ROS shutdown.
The diffboat controller configuration selects the thruster body control type, the state body-state topic and the body_command command topic.
The patrol script creates std_srvs/Empty service proxies for /gazebo/unpause_physics, /gazebo/pause_physics and /gazebo/reset_simulation.
The patrol script calls pause, then resetSimulation, then unpause as separate service calls.
The diffboat scenario launch runs the patrol node in namespace diffboat.
The patrol node publishes move_usv/goal as nav_msgs/Odometry and subscribes to move_usv/result as std_msgs/Float64.
The shipped diffboat_scenario1 scene places the diffboat at x=240, y=95, z=1.
The patrol script builds its goal Odometry with header.frame_id 'world' and position z=0.
The control documentation describes the forward-propulsion distance thresholds in meters and applies the same condition set to the differential boat.

determinism.notes: Event-driven recording stand-in with no physics step or pacing; placeholder state, thruster and result samples do not establish trajectory or state-hash replay

gaps: the fake is a ROS-free recording transport: it answers the declared goal, state, result, thruster, pause, unpause and reset endpoints and runs no Gazebo/UWSim physics, waves, wind, water current, buoyancy, thruster or boat dynamics
the state, result and thruster samples are placeholders; a live run must receive them from the operator's simulator and heading controller

the /gazebo/pause_physics, /gazebo/unpause_physics and /gazebo/reset_simulation service implementations are in gazebo_ros, outside the pinned clone; the clone proves the client endpoints and their separate use, not the callback body
the pause service freezes world stepping but does not terminate the heading controller or clear its retained target; unpausing can resume motion toward that target
the real /diffboat/state publisher belongs to the simulator deployment and may stop producing fresh samples while physics is paused; the fake still answers placeholder samples
the laser scan, camera, TF, water-current and wind-current surfaces are out of scope

mhs.safety.reset calls /gazebo/reset_simulation (gazebo_ros, outside the clone), which the shipped patrol script uses between runs to restart the scenario, so clearing the latch also resets the simulated world; the script calls unpause separately, and the heading controller keeps its retained goal
